action: Keep the application identification qualified as Thunderbird or another email-style reader unless the author confirms the exact client.
Use Evan Schwartz. The task packet says Eric, but the linked GitHub profile and gist identify Evan.
Describe Karpathy as sharing the 92-feed list as a cold start. Do not call him its curator or creator.
Attribute the underlying 2025 ranking and methodology to Michael Lynch's Hacker News Popularity Contest, then the OPML conversion to Evan Schwartz.
Keep direct quotation under the source limit and use only short phrases that the post visibly supports.
Explain that RSS enclosures predate podcasting and that current podcast feeds use them. Do not claim HobFarm publishes a podcast feed or add fake enclosures.
State the announced July 1 2013 retirement. Avoid treating the final farewell post's next-day timestamp as the service date.
Tie the removal to Firefox 64 in December 2018 and do not claim all browsers removed RSS support at once.
Say readers poll on a schedule and some systems support push. Do not promise instant delivery.
Label all three as small public projects and report repository behavior without claiming adoption, quality, or trend strength.
Name them as separate formats that readers commonly handle through the same workflow.
Audit the combined feed and all six section feeds before and after the change; test the scheduled publication boundary.
Recheck Thunderbird, NetNewsWire, Feedly, and FreshRSS steps against current official help immediately before final copy lock.
Use only original HobFarm diagrams and generated raster derivatives; record hashes and intended CDN destinations.
